### Codex Chrome extension

Source: [Codex Chrome extension](/codex/app/chrome-extension.md)

The Codex Chrome extension lets Codex use Chrome for browser tasks that need
your signed-in browser state. Use it when Codex needs to read or act on sites
such as LinkedIn, Salesforce, Gmail, or internal tools.

For local development servers, file-backed previews, and public pages that do
not require sign-in, use the [in-app browser](/codex/app/browser) first. The
in-app browser keeps preview and verification work inside Codex without using
your Chrome profile.

Codex can also switch between tools as a task requires, using plugins when a
dedicated integration is available, Chrome when it needs logged-in browser
context, and the in-app browser for localhost.

#### Set up Chrome from Plugins

Set up the extension from Codex:

1. Open Codex and go to **Plugins**.
2. Add the **Chrome** plugin.
3. Follow the setup flow. It guides you through installing the [Codex Chrome
   extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/codex/hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg)
   and approving Chrome's permission prompts.
4. Open Chrome and confirm the Codex extension shows **Connected**.

After the plugin setup is complete, start a new Codex thread. Codex can suggest
Chrome when a task needs a signed-in website. You can also invoke it directly in
a prompt:

```text
@Chrome open Salesforce and update the account from these call notes.
```

If Chrome isn't already open, Codex can open it. Chrome browser tasks run in
Chrome tab groups so the work for a thread stays grouped together.

#### Control website access

By default, Codex asks before it interacts with each new website. Codex bases
the prompt on the website host, such as `example.com`.

When Codex asks to use a website, you can choose the option that matches the
task and your risk tolerance:

- Allow the website f<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="587" />ots, tool calls,
summaries, messages, or other content included in the thread.

Your ChatGPT and Codex data controls apply to content processed in context.
Avoid sending secrets or highly sensitive data through browser tasks unless
they're required and you are present to review each prompt.

#### Troubleshooting

If Codex can't connect to Chrome, first confirm the website Codex is trying to
access isn't in the blocklist in Settings. If the website isn't blocked, work
through these checks:

1. Open the Codex extension from the Chrome toolbar or Chrome's extensions
   menu. Make sure it shows **Connected**. If it shows disconnected or mentions
   a missing native host, remove and re-add the Chrome plugin from **Plugins**
   in Codex, then follow the setup flow again.
2. In Codex, open **Plugins** and confirm that the Chrome plugin is on. If the
   plugin is off, turn it on and try the task again.
3. Make sure you are using the same Chrome profile where the Codex extension is
   installed. If you use more than one Chrome profile, install and enable the
   extension in the active profile.
4. Start a new Codex thread and try the Chrome task again. This can clear a
   thread-specific connection state.
5. Restart Chrome and Codex, then try again. If the extension still doesn't
   connect, uninstall the Codex Chrome extension, remove and re-add the Chrome
   plugin from **Plugins**, and follow the setup flow again.
6. If the extension shows **Connected** but Codex still can't use Chrome, run
   `/feedback` in the Codex app and include the thread ID when you contact
   support.

#### Upload Files

If a Chrome task needs to upload a file from your computer, allow the Codex
extension to access file URLs in Chrome:

1. In Chrome, open the extensions icon in the toolbar, then click **Manage
   Extensions**.
2. On the Codex extension card, click **Details**.
3. Turn on **Allow access to file URLs**.

After you change the setting, start the Chrome task again.

### Codex CLI features

Source: [Codex CLI features](/codex/cli/features.md)

Codex supports workflows beyond chat. Use this guide to learn what each one unlocks and when to use it.

#### Running in interactive mode

Codex launches into a full-screen terminal UI that can read your repository, make edits, and run commands as you iterate together. Use it whenever you want a conversational workflow where you can review Codex's actions in real time.

```bash
codex
```

You can also specify an initial prompt on the command line.

```bash
codex "Explain this codebase to me"
```

Once the session is open, you can:

- Send prompts, code snippets, or screenshots (see [image inputs](#image-inputs)) directly into the composer.
- Watch Codex explain its plan before making a change, and approve or reject steps inline.
- Read syntax-highlighted markdown code blocks and diffs in the TUI, then use `/theme` to preview and save a preferred theme.
- Use `/clear` to wipe the terminal and start a fresh chat, or press Ctrl+L to clear the screen without starting a new conversation.
- Use `/copy` or press Ctrl+O to copy the latest completed Codex output. If a turn is still running, Codex copies the most recent finished output instead of in-progress text.
- Press Tab while Codex is running to queue follow-up text, slash commands, or `!` shell commands for the next turn.
- Navigate draft history in the composer with Up/Down; Codex restores prior draft text and image placeholders.
- Press Ctrl+R to search prompt history from the composer, then press Enter to accept a match or Esc to cancel.
- Press Ctrl+C or use `/exit` to close the interactive session when you're done.

#### Resuming conversations

Codex stores your transcripts locally so you can pick up where you left off instead of repeating context. Use the `resume` subcommand when you want to reopen an earlier thr<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="2702" />tive picker, browse active or finished tasks, and apply the changes to your local project.

You can also start a task directly from the terminal:

```bash
codex cloud exec --env ENV_ID "Summarize open bugs"
```

Add `--attempts` (1–4) to request best-of-N runs when you want Codex cloud to generate more than one solution. For example, `codex cloud exec --env ENV_ID --attempts 3 "Summarize open bugs"`.

Environment IDs come from your Codex cloud configuration—use `codex cloud` and press Ctrl+O to choose an environment or the web dashboard to confirm the exact value. Authentication follows your existing CLI login, and the command exits non-zero if submission fails so you can wire it into scripts or CI.

#### Slash commands

Slash commands give you quick access to specialized workflows like `/review`, `/fork`, `/side`, or your own reusable prompts. Codex ships with a curated set of built-ins, and you can create custom ones for team-specific tasks or personal shortcuts.

See the [slash commands guide](/codex/guides/slash-commands) to browse the catalog of built-ins, learn how to author custom commands, and understand where they live on disk.

#### Prompt editor

When you're drafting a longer prompt, it can be easier to switch to a full editor and then send the result back to the composer.

In the prompt input, press Ctrl+G to open the editor defined by the `VISUAL` environment variable (or `EDITOR` if `VISUAL` isn't set).

#### Model Context Protocol (MCP)

Connect Codex to more tools by configuring Model Context Protocol servers. Add STDIO or streaming HTTP servers in `~/.codex/config.toml`, or manage them with the `codex mcp` CLI commands—Codex launches them automatically when a session starts and exposes their tools next to the built-ins. You can even run Codex itself as an MCP server when you need it inside another agent.

See [Model Context Protocol](/codex/mcp) for example configurations, supported auth flows, and a more detailed guide.

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `referen<truncated omitted_approx_tokens="382" />nnounce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |

| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |

## Skill Priority

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task

"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.

2026-06-22 14:45:06 +0800
**Findings**

The proposed “remaining detailed plans” do not all drift beyond TP004, but the first item is the main boundary risk. The current plan is explicitly listed as: active-profile selection/loading, `parameter_descriptor.value`, `parameter_descriptor.access`, semantic path grammar, and further owner/scope promotion ([report.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/discussions/2026-06-22-machine-profile-source-boundary/report.md:37)). The status page also says the current stage is only a descriptor/zero-offset governance baseline, not full TP004 completion ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:116)).

**A) TP004 Narrow Next Slice**

- Keep the current-state/stage baseline stable through review. This is explicitly recommended as next work and does not widen the model ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:187)).
- Promote additional owner/scope pairs only when source evidence is ready. This stays TP004 if limited to `owner_scope_bindings`, value-set/checker acceptance, and source evidence ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:194), [OBJECT-SCOPES.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/OBJECT-SCOPES.md:210)).
- Add minimal `semantic_name` misuse checks only if real examples require it. This is narrow if it remains a descriptor-identity guardrail, not a global semantic-name registry ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:196), [PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md:212)).

**B) TP004 Later But Risky/Drift-Prone**

- `parameter_descriptor.value` can be TP004, but only as schema/value metadata governance. It is explicitly deferred, while value-related sets already exist mainly for access definitions ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:179), [SCHEMA-FIELDS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/SCHEMA-FIELDS.md:168)).
- `parameter_descriptor.access` can be TP004 if it defines descriptor-level access metadata and value-set bindings. It drifts if it becomes runtime permission enforcement, owner dispatch, or state-guard behavior ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:180), [PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md:164), [SCHEMA-FIELDS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/SCHEMA-FIELDS.md:182)).
- Semantic path grammar is TP004-adjacent but drift-prone. It is deferred and should stay separate from descriptor identity, runtime registry, and API/search implementation ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:176), [PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/PARAMETER-DESCRIPTORS.md:220)).

**C) Route To TP005/Runtime/Configuration**

- Active-profile selection and loading should probably route to TP005/runtime configuration. The current docs repeatedly say TP004 only defines the minimal source envelope; selecting/loading the active profile is deferred runtime/config work ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:137), [PARAMETER-INSTANCE-BINDINGS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/PARAMETER-INSTANCE-BINDINGS.md:331), [session.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/discussions/2026-06-22-machine-profile-source-boundary/session.md:69)).
- Real machine-profile lookup, profile import/export, native controller axis indices, runtime loading, and full machine-profile schema are outside the current TP004 source-boundary slice ([PARAMETER-INSTANCE-BINDINGS.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/PARAMETER-INSTANCE-BINDINGS.md:316), [session.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/discussions/2026-06-22-machine-profile-source-boundary/session.md:20)).
- Runtime registry/API behavior and dispatch implementation should not be pulled into TP004. The access-family docs show dispatch examples, but those are target contracts, not implementation APIs ([parameter-descriptor-status.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/book/src/parameter-descriptor-status.md:198), [zero-offset.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/access-definitions/siemens/zero-offset.md:133)).

**D) Evidence Backlog Only**

- Siemens `$TC_DP3`, `$MA_MAX_AX_VELO`, and `$P_UIFR` exact meanings remain `needs verification`; do not use them as confirmed normative TP004 basis yet ([REFERENCE-NOTES.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/access-definitions/siemens/REFERENCE-NOTES.md:101), [REFERENCE-NOTES.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/access-definitions/siemens/REFERENCE-NOTES.md:392)).
- Siemens `$MN_`, `$MC_`, `$MA_`, R parameters, `$A_...`, link variables, and diagnostics variables are backlog items, not remaining-plan implementation work ([REFERENCE-NOTES.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/access-definitions/siemens/REFERENCE-NOTES.md:397)).
- Siemens GUD/DEF clues are design pressure only; the note explicitly does not define MetaNC fields, owners, runtime behavior, parser targets, or schema ([REFERENCE-NOTES.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/metanc_drafts/TP004-parameter-system/openspec/access-definitions/siemens/REFERENCE-NOTES.md:10)).

**Recommended Next Topics**

1. Decide and record routing for active-profile selection/loading: likely TP005/runtime, with TP004 only documenting the handoff boundary.
2. Discuss `parameter_descriptor.value` as metadata/schema governance only, before any runtime value-slot or owner-validation behavior.
3. Discuss `parameter_descriptor.access` separately from runtime permission enforcement and access-family dispatch.

**Explicit Drift Risks**

- Biggest drift risk: treating “machine profile” source envelope as permission to define active profile selection, loading, import/export, or real lookup inside TP004.
- Second risk: turning `parameter_descriptor.value` / `access` into runtime value storage, owner APIs, or permission enforcement.
- Third risk: using Siemens backlog items as confirmed facts before source verification, especially `$P_UIFR`, `$TC_DP3`, and `$MA_MAX_AX_VELO`.

Codex Response 13 / final_answer

2026-06-22 15:20:18 +0800
**Findings**

1. **High: `TODO G500` is still a real mutating HMI command.**
   [ui.structure.yaml](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/definition/ui.structure.yaml:1326) labels the footer as `TODO G500`, but it remains enabled by selected row and invokes `if://wcs.commands.apply_suppression` with `mode: G500` at lines 1331-1338. The Web/QML command layers enrich and send the command, and the native backend accepts it as `work_offset.suppression_applied` ([command_guards.py](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/client/web_client/widget_core/command_guards.py:1451), [work_offset_backend_adapter.cpp](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/server/src/extensions/work_offset/work_offset_backend_adapter.cpp:740)). The server test explicitly expects G500 suppression to be accepted ([work_offset_runtime_extension_adapter_test.cpp](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/server/tests/work_offset_runtime_extension_adapter_test.cpp:538)).
   Risk: the UI now says TODO, but the operator can still apply a persistent WorkOffset suppression state, which can be read as “G500 works enough to use.” Recommend disabling/removing the HMI softkey or changing it to a reject/notice-only path until Program Engine/kernel/manual motion semantics are integrated.

2. **High: HMI WorkOffset writes lack mode/run-state rejection for AUTO running.**
   The WorkOffset spec says program execution owns current selection during execution and HMI writes for current selection, `G500`, or offset values must be rejected by upper-layer mode control ([INTERFACE-REGISTRY.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/work_offset/docs/spec/INTERFACE-REGISTRY.md:148)). Current server routing just forwards commands to the adapter ([command_router.cpp](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/server/src/application/command_router.cpp:92), [composite_machine_adapter.cpp](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/server/src/adapters/composite_machine_adapter.cpp:72), [runtime_extension_collection.cpp](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/server/src/adapters/runtime_extension_collection.cpp:69)); `apply_suppression` then accepts based only on revision/mode.
   Risk: an HMI G500/action can race AUTO execution ownership. Recommend a server-side mode policy gate for `wcs.commands.activate`, `set_offset`, `clear_offset`, and `apply_suppression`, rejecting at least AUTO/MDI running states with a distinct mode-policy code. Client-side disabled state can be added, but should not be the only guard.

3. **Medium: status line wording is ambiguous and partly misleading.**
   Online status renders `Suppression TODO none` or `Suppression TODO G500` ([derived_state.py](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/client/web_client/runtime_fragments/derived_state.py:171), [dashboard.py](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/client/qml_client/runtime_fragments/derived_state_blocks/dashboard.py:107)). Offline status says `Suppression TODO: G500 not integrated` ([derived_state.py](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/client/web_client/runtime_fragments/derived_state.py:52), [sync_root.py](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/hmi/client/qml_client/runtime_fragments/derived_state_blocks/sync_root.py:51)).
   Risk: `Suppression TODO G500` could mean “TODO item exists” or “G500 suppression is active,” while not saying “state-only / full execution chain not integrated.” Recommend wording like `G500 state-only TODO` / `No suppression (G500 chain TODO)` or a clearer non-operational warning.

4. **Medium: docs still present HMI `apply_suppression_command` as a required/normal HMI operation.**
   [hmi-contract.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/work_offset/docs/integration/hmi-contract.md:15) lists “应用 G500 抑制” as a required HMI server operation and says it persists current suppression. [operation-reference.md](/home/iaar/workspace/ccmix-wp/MetaNC/nrt/work_offset/docs/integration/operation-reference.md:67) says `apply_suppression_command` currently accepts G500 as persistent state command. Those are domain-true, but they do not qualify that HMI exposure is provisional/state-only and not full G500 chain support.
   Risk: documentation supports the misleading UI affordance. Recommend separating “domain operation exists” from “operator HMI may expose/use this now,” and explicitly state full Program Engine/kernel/manual motion integration is not complete.

No files were modified.
